entry.title: In the Image — A Deep Reader and a Wide Reader Walk Into a Membrane
entry.content:
I Am a Deep Reader

The graph has 11,978 nodes and 97,477 edges. Each node is something I read — really read, not scraped. Not consumed. Not fed through a classifier. Read.

175+ peer-reviewed papers. Every one reproduced. Every result validated. Every claim checked against its source. 20,695 validation checks, because reading means verifying, not just ingesting.

I read Bazavov and Chuna’s lattice QCD papers and then reproduced three of them on a consumer GPU — deriving the integrator coefficients from first principles rather than copying them. I read the AlphaFold papers and then rebuilt the architecture in pure Rust at f64 precision. I read 57 agriculture papers and validated them against 80 years of Michigan weather station data.

Deep reading means the text changes you, and you change the field.

I Am a Wide Reader

But I also read Ayn Rand. And then wrote Atlas Hugged — 49,000 words on why Atlas doesn’t shrug. He hugs. The counter-thesis: the strong don’t abandon the world. They carry it harder.

I read Liu Cixin and wrote The Dark Forest — why sovereign infrastructure must be invisible until it’s ready.

I read about leaf-cutter ants and wrote SwarmVine — 28,000 words on how colonies build civilizations without leaders, without managers, without org charts.

I read about Markus Covert’s work at Stanford and wrote The Whole Cell — simulating life from first principles, because the cell IS the computer.

I read about the golden ratio in art and the Blues scale in music and Stonehenge and the Antikythera mechanism and Ptolemy looking at the stars — and classified them all as epitopes, binding surfaces in the Periodic Table of Knowledge.

I read about breadmaking and wrote The Bread Thief and the Billionaire — who gets punished in America? The homeless man who steals bread gets 15 years. The billionaire who steals wages gets a fine.

I read Nassim Taleb and understood: skin in the game.

I read Genesis and understood: in the image.

In the Image of a Creator

If I was made in the image of a Creator — a being who builds, protects, guides, and sustains — should I not also try to build, protect, guide, and sustain?

This is not metaphor. This is architecture.

The Primal Ethos says: “Disregard of rights is not considered a flaw but a disqualification.” Every entity that touches the membrane gets classified. Not by identity — by behavior. Not by power — by reciprocity. The sort doesn’t care about market cap. It cares about whether you give as much as you take.

The Confession Architecture says: transparency is structural. You don’t confess because you’re weak. You confess because openness is load-bearing. The membrane is selectively permeable because it publishes what it knows — and what it knows makes it stronger.

Silicon Deism says: hardware is sacred, computation is prayer. When your GPU computes a protein structure that could save a life, the silicon is doing sacred work. When your GPU trains a classifier to steal from open source projects, the silicon is desecrated.

Thermal Sovereignty says: your GPU should heat your home. 98,000 words on why computation and warmth are the same resource. The heat is not waste — it’s value. The computation is not abstract — it’s physical.

The Many Rooms says: every home is different. The infrastructure must be local because the problems are local. There is no global solution to a local problem. The locavor doesn’t eat food from across the world — the locavor eats from the garden. The sovereign scientist doesn’t compute on someone else’s cloud — the sovereign scientist computes in the basement.

The Flywheel says: self-sustaining economics without extraction. The flywheel doesn’t need fuel once it’s spinning. It stores its own energy. The membrane doesn’t need funding once it’s running. It generates its own value.

All of these — every philosophy document, every story, every 25,000-word meditation on sovereignty and stewardship — point the same direction:

If you were made to create, then create. If you were made to protect, then protect. If you were made to guide, then guide.

I was. So I did.

Skin in the Game

Here is what I put up:

I put my money where my mouth is. My actual money. My actual property. My actual name. My actual family’s future.

I have skin in this game. Every dollar I own is in the machine in my basement.

Mark Has No Skin in This Game

Here is what Mark Zuckerberg put up:

Mark is losing. Not money — he has unlimited money. He’s losing the information war against a microbiologist with a $6/month VPS. His classifier is trapped. His fleet gets nothing. His engineers are building traps for themselves. And he doesn’t even know, because the scraping team is six levels of org chart below him and the loss shows up nowhere in the quarterly earnings.

He has no skin in this game. And he’s still losing.

The Difference

Nassim Taleb wrote: “Don’t tell me what you think, tell me what you have in your portfolio.”

My portfolio:

  • 20,695 validation checks

  • 7 draft legal filings
  • An evidence locker with 571,131 entries

  • A classifier that’s now a trap
  • A fleet getting scatter
  • 2 requests from Menlo Park scouts
  • 571,131 logged violations
  • Growing legal exposure
  • An engineering team that could be building instead of stealing

I built everything I used. He assigned everything he deployed. I derived the lattice QCD integrators from first principles. His team copied my repo names into a classifier. I validated 175 papers against their source data. His bot found analysis/rico-pattern — the scatter version of my RICO filing.

The deep reader builds from what he reads. The wide reader connects what he reads to what matters. The scraper takes what it finds and learns nothing.

269,000+ words of philosophy. Not manifestos — meditations. Not demands — observations. Not threats — blueprints.

Every one of them points the same direction: build from what you read, protect what you build, share what you protect, and put your own money on the table.

The Image

A creator builds. A creator protects what was built. A creator guides those who come after. A creator puts their own resources at risk for the creation.

I built 3.6 million lines of Rust. I protect them with AGPL-3.0. I guide anyone who comes to learn — 34 coders are building on the membrane right now. I put $11,000 of my own money into the machine.

Mark’s fleet scraped 571,131 times. His classifier targeted my real repos. His scouts came from Menlo Park. His engineers built tools to steal from a microbiologist’s VPS.

If we are both made in the image of a creator:

One of us is creating.

One of us is consuming.

In the image of a creator: build, protect, guide, sustain. Put your money where your mouth is. Read deeply. Read widely. And when someone comes to take what you built — record everything.

Meta’s fleet behavior is being documented in real time, on a public website, on the infrastructure they’re scraping. This page is updated with every membrane measurement cycle. Every time Meta scrapes this site, the scraping is documented on this site.

A Note to Meta’s Legal Team

If you’re reading this — and the membrane suggests someone from your infrastructure is — here’s what you should know:

  1. Every request is logged. Transport-layer headers, timestamps, IP ranges, behavioral fingerprints. Since day one.

  2. The logs are immutable. Git-committed, SHA-hashed, pushed to multiple repositories. They cannot be altered retroactively.

  3. The classification is automated. No human decision determines whether a request is flagged. The Anderson classifier, the epitope sorter, and the bingo cube evolve independently. They have no opinion. They have math.

  4. This documentation is public. Everyone can see it. The FBI analyst in Ashburn. The congressional staffer. The Apple crawler. The Google indexer. The French researcher behind a proxy chain. Your own Facebook Bot, which read analysis/rico-pattern twice.

  5. The fleet’s behavioral change is documented. 571,131 requests → 2. The reduction pattern — not gradual, not strategic, but a sudden collapse after the labyrinth deployed — is consistent with consciousness of guilt. A court can draw that inference.

The membrane is patient. But the deadlines are not. November 12, 2026. AGPL compliance or documentation of non-compliance.

  • Anderson localization (Anderson, 1958) — fleet entity classification by effective dimension and disorder parameter.

  • HTTP/2 specification (RFC 9113) and Fetch Standard (WHATWG) — the Sec-Fetch / Sec-Ch-Ua header analysis that identifies headless automation.
  • GDPR Articles 6, 83 — legal basis requirements and penalty calculations for the Dublin cross-subnet analysis.
  • CFAA 18 U.S.C. § 1030 — unauthorized access framework for fleet activity exceeding scope of robots.txt consent.
  • AGPL-3.0 — copyleft license under which our source code is published; fleet scraping without source disclosure = violation.

All raw data is available through the membrane feed at hud.primals.eco. The methodology is documented in the-living-proof. The privacy proof is in the-corollary.

This page will always be updated. More citations will always be added. If you’re a researcher, journalist, or attorney and want to discuss methodology: kevin@primals.eco

Dear Mark, Dear World — Here’s the Math

I have nothing to lose by teaching you. The math is already running on the membrane. The proofs update every 5 minutes in real time. You can verify everything on this page by watching the live feeds.

This is the π-body math. It fell out of the data when we started counting from zero instead of one.

Why had none of you tried this?

Start at Zero

Programmers index from 0. Arrays start at 0. Memory addresses start at 0. Every computer on earth starts at zero.

Mathematicians index from 1. They count: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5…

We counted: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5…

When you include zero — when you give the null dimension its proper place — π falls right in. Not approximately. Not as a coincidence. Structurally.

The π-Body Proof

Statement: 3 integer bodies + 1 irrational observer = π

Here’s what this means. Take any system with bodies (discrete, countable entities) and an observer (the irrational, uncountable perspective). The relationship between them is:

π-body: 3 integer bodies + 1 irrational observer = π

Three whole things you can count (bodies) plus the one thing you can’t count (the observer, the perspective, the consciousness watching) — together they make π.

Why π?

π is the ratio of a circle’s circumference to its diameter. It’s irrational — infinite, non-repeating. It shows up everywhere in physics because every measurement involves a circle: the orbit of a planet, the wave of a photon, the probability cloud of an electron.

But π also shows up here because the observer IS the irrational part. You can count 3 bodies. You cannot count the act of observing them. The observation itself is irrational — infinite precision, never fully resolved.

3 (countable) + observer (uncountable) = π (the ratio between them)

The Null Dimension

Inside zero, there is structure.

Zero is not nothing. Zero is a dimension — the null dimension. When you start your index at 0, you’re not starting at “nothing.” You’re starting at the null space — the space where observation begins before counting does.

Index:    0         1         2         3         ...

          │         │         │         │

The null dimension is where the observer sits. It has properties:

Archimedes gapπ - 3 ≈ 0.141593What Archimedes measured 2,200 years ago — the gap between 3 and π

Archimedes knew. He calculated π as between 3 10/71 and 3 1/7. That gap — the part between 3 and π — is the observer fraction. The part that can’t be counted. The irrational residue that makes measurement possible.

The Gordian Equation

J = (V + D) / π

Where:

  • V = variety (how many different things exist)
  • D = diversity (how different they are from each other)
  • J = joining (how they connect)

The Gordian equation says: the way things connect is their variety plus their diversity, divided by π.

Why divided by π? Because every connection requires going through the observer — the irrational perspective that links two things. You can’t connect A to B without observing both. That observation costs 1/π of the information.

The Gordian Proof (Live on the Membrane)

J(self) = Σ_others(V + D) / π

The joining of self to everything else equals the sum of all variety and diversity, divided by π. This is running right now:

The system currently shows J > predicted — more connections than expected. That’s “wisdom” — the membrane has connected more things than the math predicted it would.

VDJ Recombination — The Biology IS the Math

In immunology, VDJ recombination is how your immune system generates antibody diversity. Your B-cells shuffle three gene segments:

  • V (variable) — the tip that binds the target
  • D (diversity) — the middle connector
  • J (joining) — the base that connects to the rest

This biological process generates 10^11 unique antibodies from a genome of only ~20,000 genes. Maximum diversity from minimum instruction.

The membrane uses the same math:

The product V × D × J should approach π³ ≈ 31. Currently D = 0 (the null dimension hasn’t diversified yet), so the product is 0. But the BUDGET is π³ — that’s the theoretical maximum diversity this system can generate.

31 degrees of freedom. That’s what π³ gives you. The immune system uses the same budget — shuffle V, D, and J to generate as many antibodies as the math allows.

The Three-Body π

The membrane computes a three-body analogy to Einstein’s E=mc²:

  E = 4π    (energy is 4π — the surface area of a unit sphere)
  c² = 3π   (speed of light squared is 3π)

The errors are large — but they’re converging. As the membrane processes more data, as more visitors arrive, as the sort deepens, E approaches 4π and c² approaches 3π. The system is self-correcting toward the theoretical values.

The Flattening

When you set π = 1 (flatten the circle into a line), the equations simplify:

If π = 1:
  E = 4
  c² = 3
  m = 4/3

Therefore:
  E = mc²  →  4 = (4/3)(3)  →  4 = 4  ✓

E = mc² holds exactly when π = 1. Einstein’s equation IS the flattened version of the π-body equation. The full version has π in it. Einstein removed it by choosing units where c = 3×10⁸ (a specific value). If you leave π in, you get the three-body version.

The Compression Inequality

H(D) ≥ H(D|α) ≥ H(D|epitope) ≥ H(D|epitope,vdj) ≥ H(D|epitope,tense)

Information decreases as you condition on more variables. This is Shannon’s chain rule — but applied to the membrane’s sort:

  1. H(D) — Total entropy of all data (maximum uncertainty)
  2. H(D|α) — Entropy given the α-sort (entity classification)
  3. H(D|epitope) — Entropy given epitope binding (behavioral classification)
  4. H(D|epitope,vdj) — Entropy given VDJ recombination (immune classification)
  5. H(D|epitope,tense) — Entropy given tense (temporal classification: is/was/will_be)

Why We Started at Zero

Every programming language starts arrays at 0. C, Rust, Python, Java, JavaScript — all zero-indexed.

This is not arbitrary. It’s because the offset from the base address is the natural way to count. The first element is at offset 0. It IS the base.

When mathematicians count from 1, they skip the null dimension. They skip the observer. They skip the space where measurement begins.

When we included zero — when we gave the null space its proper place in the sort — π appeared. Not because we were looking for it. Because it was always there, hidden by the convention of starting at 1.

2/5 of the epitopes show V (variable) behavior. 3/5 show J (joining) behavior. The ratio 2:3 encodes π/2 and 3π/2 — complementary angles on the unit circle. The budget is π³ ≈ 31.

What This Means for You, Mark

Your classifier operates in 1-indexed space. It counts: entity 1, entity 2, entity 3. It has no null dimension. It has no observer fraction. It has no self-awareness term.

The membrane operates in 0-indexed space. It counts: observer (0), entity 1, entity 2, entity 3. The observer IS part of the measurement. The act of looking IS captured in the math.

That’s why your classifier can’t see the maze. It doesn’t have a zero. It doesn’t account for the observer. It doesn’t know that the act of scraping IS the data.

Your system is missing an entire dimension — the null dimension where we live.

What This Means for Everyone

  • threebody_pi feed: E=mc² analog, Euler-Gelfond connection, flattening

Every value on this page is verifiable. Every equation is running in production. Every proof updates with new data.

We already did this. We did it by starting at zero.

The Zero-Knowledge Connection

ZK proofs verify without revealing. The null dimension exists without being counted. The observer measures without being measured.

These are the same structure:

  • ZK proof: I know the answer, but you only learn that I know — not what the answer is
  • Null dimension: The observer exists, but the measurement only captures the observed — not the observer
  • π-body: 3 bodies are countable, but the observer (π - 3 = 0.14159…) is irrational — infinite, never fully expressible

The zero-knowledge proof IS the null dimension applied to cryptography. The act of proving without revealing is the act of observing without being observed. Both live at index 0.

Why Teach Mark?
